objectives: List the notarial proceedings in Art. 569 of the Civil Procedure Code.
Decide which notary may perform a given act, depending on the location of the property.
Recognise the relations that oblige a notary to step aside.
List the breaches that make a notarial act null.
Explain what a refusal is, how it is appealed and within what time.

cards.front: Which notary issues a deed of sale of real estate?
cards.back: The notary in whose **district the property is** ([[gpk:570:1]]).

cards.front: A testator in Sofia wants a notarial will for a house in Burgas. Which notary?
cards.back: **Any** notary: wills and all acts other than real-estate deeds and certifications of ownership are not tied to the district ([[gpk:570:2]]).

cards.front: The notary's brother-in-law, the husband of the sister, is a party. Is the notary recused?
cards.back: **Not by law**: in-laws are covered only to the first degree, parents-in-law and children-in-law ([[gpk:575:1]]). The notary may still decline under [[znnd:23]] when impartiality is in doubt.
**Parties**: in whose name the act is requested. **Participants**: whose personal statements the notary certifies ([[gpk:572]]).

cards.front: Where and when may deeds for entry be issued?
cards.back: Only **in the office** and only **in working hours** ([[gpk:573:2]]).
Spouse/cohabitant; ascendants and descendants; collaterals to the **4th degree**; in-laws to the **1st degree**; guardianship, adoption, foster relations ([[gpk:575:1]]).

cards.front: Does recusal apply if the document only benefits the notary's relative?
cards.back: **Yes**, if it contains a disposition in their favour ([[gpk:575:2]]).

cards.front: Name four breaches that make a notarial act null.
cards.back: No competence or wrong district; outside the district; illegal deal; recusal; no personal appearance; no reading/signing; missing essential content; no interpreter ([[gpk:576]]).

cards.front: Where is a notary's refusal appealed?
cards.back: With a **private appeal** before the **regional court** ([[gpk:577:1]]).

cards.front: Time limit for a private appeal?
A client lends 20,000 euro and wants the fastest way to enforce if the borrower does not pay. Which form?
cards.back: A contract with **notarially certified signatures** (or a notarial deed): it allows an order for immediate enforcement, whatever the amount ([[gpk:417::3|Art. 417 item 3]] and [[gpk:418]]).
When the act is **performed**; for a circumstantial verification, when the request is **made** ([[znnd:88]]).

quiz.question: A client from Sofia owns a flat in Plovdiv and wants to sell it while staying in Sofia. Which notary issues the deed?
options: A notary of the Plovdiv district
Any notary in Sofia, where the seller lives
Any notary in Bulgaria, as for a certification
The notary chosen by the buyer, anywhere
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:570:1]]: deeds that transfer real rights in real estate are issued by the notary in whose district the property is. The seller in Sofia can sign a power of attorney at any notary ([[gpk:570:2|Art. 570(2)]]) for an agent in Plovdiv.

quiz.question: Which act may a notary in Sofia perform for a property in Varna?
options: Certify a power of attorney to sell it
Issue the sale deed for the property
Issue a declaratory deed of ownership for it
Issue a mortgage deed on the property
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:570:2]]: all acts except deeds for real rights in real estate and certifications of ownership may be performed by any notary; a power of attorney, even with certified content, is such an act. The sale, the declaratory deed and the mortgage stay in Varna ([[gpk:570:1|Art. 570(1)]]).

quiz.question: A will leaves a car to the notary's nephew, who is not a party to the act. May the notary make the will?
options: No; the act contains a disposition in favour of a relative
Yes; the nephew is not a party or a participant
Yes; a nephew is a relative of the fifth degree
Yes, if the testator signs a declaration of consent
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:575:2]]: the recusal also applies when the document contains a disposition in favour of a person of [[gpk:575:1|Art. 575(1)]]; a nephew is a collateral relative of the third degree. The testator's consent does not remove the recusal, and an act despite it is null ([[gpk:576|Art. 576]]).

quiz.question: The buyer is the notary's first cousin. May the notary issue the deed?
options: No; first cousins are collaterals of the fourth degree
Yes; cousins are not in the list of relatives of Art. 575
Yes, with the written consent of the seller
Yes, if the assistant notary signs the deed instead
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:575:1]] covers collateral relatives up to the fourth degree; first cousins are related in the fourth degree (two steps up to the common grandparents, two steps down). Consent of a party does not help, and the assistant works under the same recusal, because it attaches to the act.

quiz.question: The notary's sister-in-law (the brother's wife) is a party. Is the notary recused?
options: No; in-laws count only to the first degree
Yes; all in-laws of the notary are covered
Yes; the wife of a brother counts as a sister
Only if she lives in the notary's household
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:575:1]] covers relatives by marriage only to the first degree: parents-in-law and children-in-law. A brother's wife is a second-degree in-law, so no recusal applies by law; the notary may still decline under [[znnd:23]] when impartiality is in doubt.

quiz.question: A notary issued a sale deed for a flat in another district. What is the status of the deed?
options: Null
Valid but voidable
Valid if entered
Valid if the parties agree
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:576]]: a notarial act performed in breach of [[gpk:570:1|Art. 570(1)]], the rule on the district of the property, is null; it produces no effect, and neither the entry nor the parties' agreement cures it.

quiz.question: The seller did not come; his brother signed "for him" without a power of attorney. What is the status?
options: Null, for lack of personal appearance
Valid if the seller later confirms it
Voidable within three years by the seller
Valid, because the brother is close family
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:578:4]] requires the personal appearance of the persons whose statements the deed contains, or of their agents; a signature by a brother without a power is a breach that makes the act null ([[gpk:576|Art. 576]]). A later confirmation does not revive a null act.

quiz.question: Within what time can a client appeal the notary's refusal?
options: One week from the notification
One month from the notification
Two weeks from the notification
Three days from the notification
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:577:1]]: a refusal is appealed with a private appeal before the regional court; [[gpk:275:1|Art. 275(1)]] sets one week from the notification for a private appeal. The office gives the refusal in writing with its date, so the client can keep the term.

quiz.question: The regional court sets aside a refusal of an entry. When is the entry deemed made?
options: From the moment of the request for entry
From the date of the court decision
From the date of a new request after the decision
From the next working day after the decision
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:577:3]]: when the court sets aside a refusal of an entry, the entry is deemed made from the moment of the request. The rank of the act is thus kept against acts entered in the meantime ([[zs:113]]).

quiz.question: A patient in hospital needs a power of attorney certified today. Is it possible?
options: Yes; outside the office for good reasons, with an added fee
No; every notarial act is performed only in the office
Yes, but only outside working hours and on weekends
Only if the patient sends a relative with the document
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:573:3]]: acts other than deeds subject to entry may be performed outside the office and out of hours when good reasons prevent the person from coming; [[tarifa:23|item 23 of the tariff]] adds 25% for an act outside the office in working hours. A relative cannot sign for the patient ([[gpk:578:4|Art. 578(4)]]).

quiz.question: Why do lenders prefer a loan contract with notarially certified signatures?
options: It allows an order for immediate enforcement
It lowers the statutory interest on the loan
It frees the loan from the tax on interest
It is required by law for every loan
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:417::3|Art. 417 item 3 ГПК]]: a notarial deed, a settlement or another contract with notarially certified signatures about an obligation to pay money allows the creditor to ask for an order for immediate enforcement ([[gpk:418|Art. 418]]), whatever the amount. Interest and tax do not change.

quiz.question: When does the client pay the fee for a circumstantial verification?
options: When the request is made; not returned on refusal
After the deed is issued, with the copies
Only if the ownership is recognised by the notary
At the end of the year, with the other fees
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:88:1]]: fees are due when the act is performed, but the fee for a circumstantial verification is due when the request is made; the note to [[tarifa:11|item 11 of the tariff]] adds that it is not returned when ownership is not recognised.
